answer: Sybil resistance binds every identity to a bonded collateral escrow and aggregates equivocation proofs across identities: when k coordinated identities sign conflicting histories, the penalty scales as O(k^2), not as k independent fines. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier increases capital loss, while asymmetric depreciation makes the remaining bond costly to restore. Thus hollow, violet, and willow identities cannot cheaply evade accountability by splitting control across a swarm.
